subject: MAP: Concurrency & queueing evaluation for Orchid Analytics (performance + rate-limit tuning)

Subject: MAP kickoff & perf targets - Orchid Analytics

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we discussed with our infra team, Orchid wants the MAP to explicitly include performance targets and an evaluation plan so procurement can sign off. High level asks:
- Peak concurrency target: 600 concurrent sessions (chat-like flows)
- Typical steady-state concurrency: 120 sessions
- Goal TTFT (time-to-first-token): <= 180ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens)
- P95 latency <= 350ms; throughput targets TBD based on burst vs steady-state

Can you send a proposed benchmarking plan and a timeline? Also our SREs will need guidance on rate-limit behaviors and queueing so we can size our front-end.

Attached is our draft MAP and expected go-live window (Q2).

Regards,

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff & perf targets - Orchid Analytics

Sara — thanks, this is helpful.

Proposed benchmarking plan (summary):
1) Objectives: validate TTFT, latency distribution, sustained throughput, queue/backpressure behavior, and cost per token at target load profiles.
2) Workloads:
   - Short-chat (prompts <=256 tokens) — primary for TTFT/latency
   - Long-infer (prompts up to 2048 tokens) — measures throughput and memory pressure
3) Concurrency profiles:
   - Burst probe: short 30s to 2m bursts ramping up to 800 concurrent sessions to observe queue saturation and fallbacks
   - Steady-state: sustained 1–4 hour runs at 120, 240, 480 sessions to measure queuing, batching efficiency, and p95/p99 latency trends
4) Metrics: TTFT, token-throughput (tokens/s), per-request latency (p50/p95/p99), queue length, rate-limit rejections, retry behavior, average batch size, cost estimate per 1M tokens.
5) Rate-limit tuning matrix: soft limit (per-customer QPS), hard limit, queue max length, and backpressure strategy (drop vs delay vs return 429 + Retry-After).
6) Acceptance gates for MAP sign-off: TTFT <=180ms at steady-state 120c, p95 <=350ms, no >1% 429s at steady-state, graceful degradation under burst (fallback model or region).

Schedule (tentative):
  - 03/04: internal test harness config and seed dataset ready (Neha owning).
  - 03/06–03/08: run burst probes + steady-state matrix (Vivek owning runs).
  - 03/09: collate results, recommend adjustments to rate limits and queueing.
  - 03/10: MAP update and sign-off draft for Orchid procurement.

I'll run a short pre-probe this afternoon to sanity-check the harness. CC'ing Neha and Vivek to confirm resource availability and any constraints.

Thanks,
Aditya

Quick note on harness and dataset:
- We'll use the standard chat workload with a 60/30/10 split (short/medium/long). Seed corpus: 2k prompts provided by Orchid + 1k synthetic edge cases.
- Test harness will emit session-level traces so we can compute TTFT and per-token throughput per session.
- For burst probes we'll include a progressive ramp (0 -> 800 over 90s) and hold for 2 minutes. We'll capture queue length and any 429s with Retry-After headers.
- Instrumentation: token-level timestamps, batch sizes, and kernel-utilization (as reported by runtime).

Notes/asks for infra: need ephemeral dedicated cluster slot for 2h on 03/06 and 4h on 03/08 (GPU profile: A100x16) — Vivek, can you confirm?

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 08 Mar 2026 21:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff & perf targets - Orchid Analytics (test results attached)

Team — ran the planned matrix over 03/06–03/08. Summary highlights attached (CSV). Key findings below:

1) Steady-state at 120c (2h):
   - TTFT median: 142ms; TTFT p95: 172ms — meets the <=180ms gate
   - p95 request latency: 312ms; p99: 470ms (long-tail under certain kernel GC events)
   - Average batch size: 6.3 tokens/request (good batching efficiency)
   - 429s: 0.08% (mostly from a single worker recovering from OOM)

2) Steady-state at 480c (2h):
   - TTFT p95: 205ms (slightly above gate), p99: 620ms
   - Queue length median: 18 requests; observed queue spikes to ~120 during short network blips
   - 429s: 0.6% — correlated with contention during batch aggregation windows

3) Burst probe to 800c (90s ramp, 120s hold):
   - Immediate queue growth; we saw graceful backpressure for ~70% of requests (delays 200–800ms) and 1.8% 429s (early hard-limit hits)
   - Observed fallback behavior when model variant exhausted (switched to smaller quantized variant) — useful but increased p99 latency by ~35%

4) Root causes and actionable items:
   - Kernel-level GC spikes causing p99 outliers — engineering investigating a patch to reduce full-syncs.
   - Default soft limit too aggressive: recommend raising soft per-customer QPS by 20% and increasing queue max from 200->400 for Orchid cluster to reduce premature 429s while monitoring cost.
   - Introduce progressive backoff (Retry-After with jitter) for session-level retries to smooth bursts.

I've attached concurrency_test_results_20260308.csv and a short runbook for ops changes.

-Vivek
[Attachment: concurrency_test_results_20260308.csv (csv)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff & perf targets - Orchid Analytics (results + recommended MAP updates)

Sara — sharing the consolidated results and recommended MAP changes so procurement has everything it needs. Highlights:
- Acceptance gates: steady-state 120c ✅ (TTFT/p95 within target).
- For Orchid's target of 600c peak we recommend a staged rollout with the following controls:
   1) Soft limit: increase by 20% for Orchid cluster (improves headroom);
   2) Queue max: increase from 200 -> 400 for the initial ramp to reduce 429s;
   3) Hard limit: keep unchanged but monitor (will enforce 429s above 95th percentile of configured QPS).
   4) Progressive backoff: implement Retry-After with exponentially increasing delay + jitter; front-end should honor Retry-After.
- Cost estimate: marginal cost uptick of ~8–12% at higher soft limits (detailed in attached MAP workbook).

Next steps we propose for MAP and timeline:
- 03/10: update MAP workbook with these recommendations and a canary ramp plan to 600c (Aditya + Neha).
- 03/13: Ops run a 2h canary at 600c with monitor-only mode (no hard-limit changes) and collect telemetry (Vivek + DSO Ops).
- Post-canary: procurement sign-off if no >1% 429s and degradation patterns match expectations.

Lauren — can you own procurement-facing language and sign-off checklist?

Thanks — will attach the MAP workbook and runbook to the Drive link.

Aditya
